newsitem.title: USA: COMEX presses on with Chile warehouse plan.
newsitem.headline: COMEX presses on with Chile warehouse plan.

text.p: The New York Mercantile Exchange's COMEX division is pressing on with its plan to open a copper warehouse in Chile to take delivery of its red metal futures contract despite differing views within and outside the exchange over the way forward.
COMEX chairman John Moore said the copper industry was still divided over the issue and a round of talks with producers in the South West will take place later this month.
"There are people for and people against it, but I am not getting calls saying don't do it," Moore said.
The exchange should stick to having just one copper contract rather than launching a second, parallel contract for delivery outside the U.S., Moore believed.
"Personally I do not believe that two contracts would survive. I do not believe you can trade two contracts," he said.
A sub-committee has been created to push forward with the Chile project, backed by money from NYMEX.

"The LME trades one copper contract and they have delivery points all over the world and that seems to somehow or other have worked," Moore added. "They have no fixed discounts or premiums. In my mind the market sorts that out."

A senior sales official for a U.S. copper producer said a Chilean warehouse was a bad idea because it could dilute COMEX as a price reference for the United States, but it may work if a second contract was launched.
The vast majority of physical copper sales in the U.S., including scrap, are priced basis COMEX.
NYMEX president Patrick Thompson told Reuters during Copper Club week mid-February that the exchange's thinking was moving towards launching a second copper contract for foreign delivery points.

"We believe we would probably not open warehouses for delivery against our current contract. It may entail having a separate futures contrat that would trade in parallel with the existing futures contract," Thompson said at the time.
Moore said the COMEX copper committee would come up with proposals but it would be up to the membership of the exchange to vote on the outcome.
